issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slow or erratic shifts, a flashing D4 light with the check engine light, sudden downshifts to second gear at highway speed, slipping, or no drive at all.
issues.why: The 5-speed automatic in the second-generation CL wears out early. Acura extended the transmission warranty to 7 years or 100,000 miles on 2001-2002 and some 2003 CLs, and failure is by far the most reported problem.
issues.next: If the D4 light flashes or shifts get rough, change the fluid with genuine Honda/Acura ATF and get a diagnosis right away. A sudden downshift at speed is dangerous, so don't put this off. Most failed units need a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Second gear can break from overheating (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before failure. In the worst case the transmission locks up while driving.
issues.why: Heat builds up between two second-gear parts inside the automatic transmission, which can chip or break gear teeth.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer adds a fluid line change on low-mileage cars, or inspects the gears and replaces the transmission if overheating damage is found.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifting problems and failure
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, flaring revs between gears, or the car not moving in drive.
issues.why: Automatic transmission complaints are among the most common for the first-generation CL, with some owners needing more than one transmission.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't engage, stop driving hard and have the transmission diagnosed before more damage is done.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. You may have received a recall letter.
issues.why: The original Takata driver airbag inflator, and some replacement inflators fitted later, can absorb moisture and rupture in a crash, throwing metal fragments.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and get the free inflator replacement now, even if an earlier airbag recall was done.

issues.t: Older driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. You may have received a recall letter.
issues.why: Driver airbag inflators used in 1996-2001 Honda and Acura models can absorb moisture over time, which can make them rupture or underinflate in a crash.
issues.next: Look up your VIN and have the dealer inspect and replace the inflator for free.

issues.t: Engine stalls from worn ignition switch (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off without warning while driving, or the car won't start; jiggling the key may bring power back.
issues.why: Electrical contacts inside the ignition switch wear out and lose connection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the free ignition switch replacement done. If it stalls, steer to safety; steering and brakes get heavier with the engine off.

issues.t: Key comes out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can turn off the car and remove the key without the shifter being fully in Park, and the car may roll away.
issues.why: Wear in the ignition key cylinder lets the shift interlock stop working.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN and have the dealer inspect and replace the worn interlock parts for free.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints wear out (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, loose steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case the joint separates and the front wheel collapses.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on these cars could wear out early.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall, and have the ball joints inspected if you hear clunks. Do not drive a car with a loose ball joint.

issues.t: Car can roll while in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car moves or rolls down a slope even though the shifter is in Park.
issues.why: A casting flaw in a transmission cover could stop the parking pawl from locking the transmission on some 1998 2.3CL automatics.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park. Check your VIN for the recall; dealers add a collar so the parking pawl engages properly.

issues.t: Timing belt can break from misaligned pulley (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or ticking from the front of the engine, then the engine stalls and won't restart if the belt breaks.
issues.why: On some 2003 V6 engines, a misaligned water pump pulley let the timing belt rub on a cylinder head bolt until it broke. This engine can suffer internal damage when the belt fails.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Dealers inspect the water pump and replace it and the timing belt if needed.

issues.t: Airbag (SRS) light on
issues.sym: The SRS airbag warning light stays on or flickers.
issues.why: Owners trace it to a faulty seat belt buckle switch, a failed SRS control module or wiring problems. While the light is on, airbags may not deploy.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read by a shop with the right scan tool. Fix it promptly, because the airbags may be disabled.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause vibration
issues.sym: Vibration through the seat and steering wheel at idle in gear or around highway speed, and a clunk when shifting or accelerating.
issues.why: The rubber and fluid-filled engine mounts wear out with age. Owners report replacing front and side mounts.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked. Replace broken mounts soon, because they let the engine move and strain hoses, axles and other mounts.

issues.t: Rusted front subframe on passenger side
issues.sym: Clunks or creaks from the front, odd steering feel, or a failed inspection for rust. The subframe can rust through near the control arm mounts.
issues.why: Owners report heavy subframe rust on the passenger side, which they link to air conditioner condensation dripping onto it, made worse by road salt.
issues.next: Have the subframe inspected on a lift, especially in salt states. Badly rusted subframes need replacing, since a failure can affect steering.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start when hot
issues.sym: On hot days or after a drive, the engine cranks but won't fire. After it cools down it usually starts again.
issues.why: Owners have traced this to a failing fuel pump or fuel injection (main) relay that loses contact when warm, cutting power to the fuel pump.
issues.next: When it happens, have a shop check for fuel pump power and spark. Replacing the relay is a cheap common fix.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak and pump whine
issues.sym: Whining from the engine bay when turning, especially when cold, and power steering fluid spots or low fluid.
issues.why: Old O-rings and hoses in the power steering system leak or let air in. Using the wrong fluid also causes pump noise.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and use only Honda power steering fluid. Replace leaking O-rings or hoses before the pump runs dry.

issues.t: HID headlight flickering or going out
issues.sym: One low-beam headlight flickers, changes color or goes dark.
issues.why: The high-intensity discharge (HID) bulbs and their ballasts wear out with age.
issues.next: Swap the bulbs side to side to see if the problem follows the bulb or stays with the ballast, then replace the faulty part. Replace bulbs in pairs so the color matches.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coil
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, a stumble when accelerating, and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: One of the six individual ignition coils fails and stops firing its cylinder.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read to find the cylinder. Replace the bad coil and check the spark plugs; avoid hard driving with a flashing light, which can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Front axle failure or vibration
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, vibration under acceleration, or an axle that breaks or pops out.
issues.why: Owners report worn or rusted front CV axles, and broken axles on hard acceleration.
issues.next: Have the axles and boots inspected if you hear clicking. Replace a worn axle before it breaks and leaves you stranded.

issues.t: Brake vibration or noise from rusted rotors
issues.sym: Pulsing in the brake pedal or steering wheel when stopping, grinding or scraping noise, or brakes that drag.
issues.why: Rotors rust and wear unevenly, and caliper brackets can corrode.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. New rotors and pads, plus cleaning or replacing corroded hardware, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Auto-dimming mirror leaks dark fluid
issues.sym: A black, tar-like fluid drips from the rearview mirror onto the console or seats, and the mirror may stop dimming.
issues.why: The gel inside the self-dimming mirror leaks out as the mirror's seal fails.
issues.next: Avoid touching the fluid with bare skin, clean it up, and replace the mirror.

issues.t: Check engine light for EVAP leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on but the car drives normally.
issues.why: A worn fuel cap seal or a failed valve or sensor near the charcoal canister lets fuel vapor escape.
issues.next: Replace the fuel cap first if its seal is cracked. If the light returns, have the EVAP system tested.

issues.t: Check engine light from clogged EGR passages
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0401, sometimes with pinging or hesitation.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the EGR valve and intake passages until too little exhaust gas flows.
issues.next: Have the EGR valve and passages cleaned and the gasket replaced. This is a common, moderate repair.

issues.t: Driver power window stops working
issues.sym: The driver window won't go up or down, or moves slowly.
issues.why: The power window motor fails, sometimes more than once.
issues.next: Have the motor and switch tested. Replacing the motor (and regulator if worn) fixes it.

issues.t: Speedometer reads slower than actual speed
issues.sym: The speedometer shows a lower speed than you are really going.
issues.why: Owners report the speedometer reading slow; a failing speed sensor or gauge is the usual cause.
issues.next: Check your speed with a phone GPS app and have the speed sensor and gauge tested. Wrong readings can lead to tickets.

issues.t: Starter fails to crank the engine
issues.sym: A click or nothing at all when you turn the key, even though the lights work.
issues.why: Starter and ignition parts are a common complaint on these cars. Corroded battery terminals can cause the same symptom.
issues.next: Clean and tighten the battery terminals first. If it still won't crank, have the starter and ignition switch tested.
